hits.text:
All code is slop, except mine

That’s what Lauren Tan, the engineer behind Grok Bot, said on stage

She ships 3,000+ pull requests a month, and her secret is what she does every time an agent makes a mistake

Most people just add another line to AGENTS.md

Lauren runs every mistake through 4 questions instead:

> Can I redesign the code so this mistake is impossible?
> Can a lint rule or a type catch it automatically?
> Can the agent catch it by running and checking its own work?
> Does it really need a written rule?

Each mistake gets one of 5 fixes:

Redesign / lint / verify / write a rule / human review

The useful part is that a written rule is only one option, not the default

Most of her fixes never touch AGENTS.md at all

> Sometimes the answer is to ban something entirely, like useEffect
> Sometimes it’s a lint rule: her team went from 7 to 167 of them in four months
> Sometimes it’s letting the agent prove its work with screenshots

Mistake -> cheapest permanent fix -> never catch it by hand again

virals.text:
🚨 OPENAI JUST TOOK A MAJOR STEP INTO AGENTIC PAYMENTS

OpenAI announced ChatGPT Wallet, allowing AI agents to make purchases on behalf of users.

Here's how it works:

Tell your AI agent what you want to buy.
The agent researches products, compares prices, and prepares checkout.
You approve the transaction.
The agent completes payment without accessing your actual card details.

Initially, every purchase requires approval. But OpenAI envisions a future where agents can spend autonomously within predefined limits.

WHY THIS MATTERS

We're moving toward an economy where AI agents don't just recommend products. They actually execute financial transactions.

Today, OpenAI uses traditional card networks, including Visa and Mastercard.

But as agentic commerce scales, it could create enormous opportunities for payment networks, stablecoins, and blockchain settlement infrastructure.

The big question: Who will capture the financial activity when AI agents start transacting at scale?

#OpenAI #AgenticPayments #AI #Crypto

virals.text:
Goldman Sachs restricted Claude Code and GitHub coding tools mostly to engineers in October.

In July its CIO Marco Argenti praised non-developers using AI for vibe coding. Traders built tools for client trade-flow monitoring, market and position modeling, and text or graphics work. Engineers then refined those tools.

The bank ran a trial. 
It weighed productivity against risk. 
The October guidance limits the tools to engineers. Strats who mix trading, quant work and engineering stay exempt. Some traders complained.

A Goldman spokesperson said the evaluation looked at productivity and risk management. It will keep the tools with the employees best suited for longer use.

How much of the trader-built workflow actually survives once only engineers can keep building it?

outsiders.text:
Goldman Sachs restricted Claude Code and GitHub coding tools mostly to engineers in October.

In July its CIO Marco Argenti praised non-developers using AI for vibe coding. Traders built tools for client trade-flow monitoring, market and position modeling, and text or graphics work. Engineers then refined those tools.

The bank ran a trial. 
It weighed productivity against risk. 
The October guidance limits the tools to engineers. Strats who mix trading, quant work and engineering stay exempt. Some traders complained.

A Goldman spokesperson said the evaluation looked at productivity and risk management. It will keep the tools with the employees best suited for longer use.

How much of the trader-built workflow actually survives once only engineers can keep building it?
